records.text: An anonymous federal-court employee wrote that, in every federal court where they had worked, video and photo evidence was never altered because presenting modified evidence to a jury would be prejudicial.
records.speaker: Federal court employee email source (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: Please do not mention my name or identity. in any way, but I can tell you categorically that in every federal court that I have worked in, video and photo evidence is never altered in any way as it would be considered prejudiced to present it to the jury if it has been modified in any way. I just wanted to let you know this. Best of luck with your continued investigation.

verification.notes: Transcript context was reviewed and live searches were performed for federal-court evidence guidance and the quoted wording. The episode is the only source for the private message. Because the sender is anonymous, their federal-court employment and claimed experience cannot be authenticated, and the categorical practice claim cannot be tested against identified courts or cases. The message is therefore attempted/unverifiable rather than false.
